# `in` standard library

**Audience:** Edva command-line programs<br>
**Status:** current reference<br>
**Audited:** `8b8cb19`<br>
**Evidence:** `std/in.dva`, `std/io.dva`

`in` provides a shared buffered reader over standard input. Every operation
returns an optional ram: the positive slot carries data, and the unit second
slot indicates EOF.

| Function | Result | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `read_line(max)` | `< String | >` | read through newline; remove trailing carriage return |
| `read_bytes(max)` | `< String | >` | read at most `max` available bytes |
| `read_byte!` | `< Int | >` | read one byte |
| `read_until(delim, max)` | `< String | >` | read through and consume `delim` |

```dva
#use in

line = in::read_line(4096)
line | text => print(text) | _ => print("end of input")
```

The reader is module-global, so calls share buffering and advance the same
standard-input stream. Use `io::reader(fd)` directly when a program needs a
separate reader or a descriptor other than standard input.
